newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Havel's health improving after operation - doctors.
newsitem.headline: Havel's health improving after operation - doctors.

text.p: Czech President Vaclav Havel's health is steadily improving after surgery nine days ago to remove a small malignant tumour from one lung, and he was able to drink a little Czech beer, doctors said on Tuesday.
Doctors said there was no evidence of the cancer spreading to other tissue after the operation, which removed half of his right lung.
"One can't be 100 percent sure but the prognosis looks very hopeful," Dr. Ctibor Povysil, who conducted a microscopic examination of the tumour, told a news conference.

Havel has been on a respirator since the operation. A tracheotomy to install the respirator through his throat was performed last Thursday as his breathing problems worsened. He is expected to be off the respirator by the end of the week.
Havel, aged 60 and a heavy smoker, entered the Third Surgical Clinic in central Prague on November 25 after his office said he had been suffering from pneumonia.
The former dissident playwright who helped lead Prague's "Velvet Revoution" that toppled communism has limited executive powers as president, and has not relinquished any of his duties.
